newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids mostly hold with hot weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids mostly hold with hot weather.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices were unchanged to up slightly Tuesday in moderate activity, with firmer gas prices and hot East Coast weather boosting prospects for better utility demand, sources said.

"Our burns have been sky high because of the heat and the nuke outages, and we have been burning oil because it's cheaper than gas," said one East Coast utility buyer, noting city gate gas prices jumped sharply this week with the heat.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent held relatively steady at $16.00-25 a barrel, with July paper also pegged little changed at $16.10-25, traders said.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour again edged up slightly to the $17.75 area, again boosted by prospects for better cooling demand amid fairly limited supply, traders said.
High sulphurs in New York were unchanged, with 2.2 percent still seen at $14.50-75..
Traders said a New York utility was looking for a cargo of 1.5 percent material for July 7 delivery.

In the East, unplanned nuclear unit outages were reported this week at PECO's 1,055 MW Limerick 1, GPU's 786 MW Three Mile Island 1 and Duke's 846 MW Oconee 3, and all were expected to remain off line for most of the week.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent was steady to up slightly at $15.75-16.00, while three percent notionally held steady at $13.50-75, traders said.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.

New York city gate swing gas prices gained about a nickel Tuesday to the low-$2.60s/mmBtu, or $16.57 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, was talked two cents higher at $2.31/mmBtu, or $14.55 a barrel.
